page: Vultr voc-m-24c-192gb-2400s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 12 physical AMD EPYC cores with multithreading enabled. The system architecture is x86_64, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is provided locally via a 2400 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations place the server's single-core CPU performance in the top tier (top 10%) via stress-ng, while multi-core CPU performance ranks in the top 25%. Memory performance is highly competitive, with the PassMark memory score reaching the top 10% and large-block read/write memory bandwidth scoring in the top 25%. In language model workloads, the server achieves top-tier text generation speeds of 348.95 tokens per second for small 135M models, and strong text generation speeds of 35.13 tokens per second for medium 7B models.

Given the dedicated AMD EPYC processor allocation and the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server offers high resource density for memory-intensive workloads. The inclusion of a large 2400 GB NVMe SSD provides local storage capacity without requiring external block storage attachments, enhancing qualitative cost efficiency for data-heavy deployments. This configuration is suitable for memory-optimized databases, medium-scale language model inference, image processing, and multi-threaded text processing workloads.
description: Vultr voc-m-24c-192gb-2400s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor with 24 dedicated vCPUs, 12 physical cores, and a 2.0 GHz clock speed. It features 192.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU memory ratio, and includes a 2400 GB local NVMe SSD. In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates top-tier single-core CPU performance and memory scores, alongside strong multi-core execution and large-block memory bandwidth. Text generation for small language models also reaches top-tier speeds, while medium model generation remains strong. Lacking a GPU, the server relies on its dedicated AMD EPYC architecture and high memory capacity to handle demanding workloads. This hardware profile is optimized for memory-intensive databases, text and image processing, and local language model inference.
